correctness.rationale: Exact local formula gives beta(m) even iff odd m is nonsquare; for u=beta(2^a m) the 2-adic factor ratio is at most 3/4, at most 11/16 away from valuation 2, and a 3-factor ratio is at most 7/9. The a odd, a=2 and a even>=4 branches all contradict beta(u)=n/2, the last branch using 3|beta(u) to force 3|m. The disjoint square/twice-square count follows exactly. The independent Liouville-formula cross-check and sieve through 10^6 passed; finite checks are corroborative.

originality.rationale: Tóth 2011 §§2,7,8 supplies the local beta identities, parity lemma, six witnesses and an explicit open question about further superimperfect integers, but does not prove beta(n) must be odd at a superimperfect input or derive a uniform O(sqrt X) counting bound. OEIS A200758 gives a finite table and searches. Eight targeted published-finding corpus semantic searches and targeted web searches for aliases/shape bounds yielded no covering theorem; the closest records use distinct arithmetic functions and do not imply the result. Residual unindexed overlap is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Prior unindexed or informal arguments might establish the same necessary condition; literature screening cannot certify absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: Tóth explicitly poses the existence of other beta-superimperfect numbers as an open problem. An unrestricted necessary shape theorem rules out every input with nonsquare odd part and yields a uniform square-root counting bound; this is a substantive global sparsity constraint, not merely a restatement of the known parity rule or list of examples.
